articles.title: Epic Reveals Drop Rate for Fortnite's Pirate Token Following Pressure From Fans
articles.summary: Epic Games has revealed the drop rate for Fortnite's Pirate Token after backlash surrounding the infamous in-game pickup saw fans try to report the studio to the FTC.
body: It's been just one week since Epic turned the Item Shop on its head with the launch of its Treasure Hunters mini-season November 1. At the center of the backlash is the Pirate Token, an ultra-rare drop that grants access to the Pirate Shop and effectively makes just about every item in the shop free for 14 days.

It's an in-game collectible with unprecedented value, so naturally, it's sent players into a frenzy as they turn over every chest in hopes of finding one for themselves. The problem with a token like this, players have argued, is that they should probably be made aware of the odds of actually finding it so they don't gamble their time on chests that could very likely never yield results. It's transparency that Epic has failed to provide – until now.
points: Epic Games has revealed the drop rate for Fortnite's Pirate Token after backlash surrounding the infamous in-game pickup saw fans try to report the studio to the FTC.

articles.title: 68 Years Later, Peanuts’ Most Mysterious Character Is Finally Making Her Official Debut — But There's a Catch
articles.summary: There are some elements of Charles Schulz's Peanuts comic that have hardly aged at all, such as the characters' relationships or its focus on team sports. Most kids in America, before or since, have had the experience of being on a team where one kid is taking the game way too seriously while…
body: Other parts of Peanuts, on the other hand, are portraits of a bygone era. If you're younger than about 45, you probably never had an old-school "pen pal." These were kids in other states or countries who you'd send handwritten letters, either as a learning or social exercise. Depending on how you look at it, the advent of the home internet either destroyed the practice on the spot or ensured that "pen pals" now make up a solid 50% of a modern kid's social circle.

Both Charlie Brown and his sister Sally would periodically write to various pen-pals over the course of the next 36 years, with Charlie Brown occasionally trying to do so in ink. Readers almost never saw either Charlie Brown or Sally get a letter in return, although Schulz established in the first week of the bit that Charlie Brown’s anonymous "pencil-pal" was from somewhere outside the United States.
points: There are some elements of Charles Schulz's Peanuts comic that have hardly aged at all, such as the characters' relationships or its focus on team sports.

articles.title: Bethesda's Most Reviled Game Becomes a 10/10 If You Ignore the Story
articles.summary: Recently, Bethesda dominated conversations simply by announcing that the long-awaited Elder Scrolls 6 has an official subtitle: Sentinel. We didn’t learn much more than that, but it was enough to keep us talking because that’s the sort of hold Bethesda has on us. Sometimes.
body: Starfield, launched Sep. 6, 2023, represented a rare loosening of that grip. Despite offering the sort of sprawling environments for which Bethesda is known, the game was met with a collective shrug from much of its potential audience. We’d been there, done that — or so we thought. Comparisons to No Man’s Sky, which launched to similarly disappointing reviews before righting the ship, seemed only natural. No one seemed to love the game and its story. And yet, if you skip the story and find other ways to amuse yourself, Starfield is pretty much a ten out of ten.

Our expectations were part of the problem. Ahead of the game’s release, we looked forward to a vast universe populated by dozens memorable characters, telling entertaining stories about the time they took an arrow to the knee. Given the change in setting, maybe they would survive a blaster shot to the elbow? I could see that.
points: Recently, Bethesda dominated conversations simply by announcing that the long-awaited Elder Scrolls 6 has an official subtitle: Sentinel.

articles.title: LEGO Black Friday 2026 Sales: What to Expect
articles.summary: On nearly every IGN article about LEGO sets (and as the LEGO editor here at IGN, I post a lot of them), commenters complain that LEGO sets cost too much. That’s a fair criticism, especially because many of the most noteworthy LEGO sets are expensive.
body: Even the smaller sets cost more than you might expect if you don’t pay attention to the market. They’re comprised of many tiny interlocking pieces, after all. If you feel like you’re priced out of many LEGO sets you’d want to buy, Black Friday offers an excellent opportunity to buy them at some of the lowest prices of the year.
The question is, what kinds of discounts on LEGO can we expect to see this Black Friday? I’ve been covering LEGO deals for many years now, so here’s what I expect based on my experience.

Many times throughout the year, LEGO sets go on sale at various retailers. These run-of-the-mill sales generally offer discounts of 20% off. That’s the standard sale price at retailers like Amazon, Target, Best Buy, and the LEGO Store.
Therefore, a particularly good sale on LEGO sets is when you can find them for 30%, 40%, or even 50% off. These are the kinds of discounts I expect to see once the true Black Friday sales begin.

body: Though Taylor-Joy’s remarkable range and phenomenal acting have earned widespread admiration, one role in particular won the hearts of families everywhere. This sci-fi film revealed a fresh comedic side of her talent, adding another dimension to her on-screen performances. It also became one of the greatest animated achievements of all time, the second-highest-grossing animated film of 2026.
What film could we possibly be talking about? The Super Mario Galaxy Movie, of course. And it's coming to Netflix later this month on Nov. 30.

Directed by the creative minds behind Teen Titans Go! (Aaron Horvath and Michael Jelenic), The Super Mario Galaxy Movie is a thrilling action-comedy based on Nintendo's Mario video game franchise (created by Shigeru Miyamoto) and produced by Illumination and Nintendo.

articles.title: Sydney Sweeney’s Extremely R-Rated 131-Minute Thriller Is Officially Streaming on HBO
articles.summary: Despite its overwhelming commercial success, Freida McFadden’s psychological thriller, The Housemaid, is far from a perfect read. Trope-heavy and full of obvious contrivances, The Housemaid sets up a tense domestic thriller premise that is meant to be consumed as a fast-paced popcorn novel.
body: Bridesmaids director Paul Feig’s The Housemaid lives up to these expectations. Formulaic but utterly entertaining, the film features Sydney Sweeney and Amanda Seyfried as characters that seem to be pitted against each other. The Housemaid is a great fit for anyone who likes erotic thrillers of the Verity variety, wherein the plot features some sort of unexpected twist to keep things interesting. If you’ve been meaning to watch The Housemaid from the comfort of your home, the film is available to stream on HBO Max right now.

Recently paroled Millie (Sweeney) tries to put her past behind her by working as a live-in maid for Nina (Seyfried), who lives with her husband, Andrew (Brandon Sklenar), and daughter, Cece (Indiana Elle). Nina needs help because she is pregnant, and Millie needs to maintain a lawful employment status, making the arrangement feasible at first. Nina’s suburban mansion in Great Neck, Long Island, is opulent to the point of appearing gaudy, giving Millie all the more reason to commit to the job seriously.

articles.title: Missing Teen Saved From Alleged Kidnapper After Seeking Help in Among Us
articles.summary: A Utah teenager was rescued from an Oregon man's home after she successfully contacted help from another child in Among Us. Authorities saved the 17-year-old November 1, 2026, after receiving a tip relayed by a younger player she met while playing developer Innersloth's hit party mystery game…
body: The Utah teen was just 15 when she was reported missing in May 2025. Harmel allegedly began contacting her through Snapchat earlier that month before offering to send her money to travel to his home in Oregon. He then made the hours-long drive to her location and lured her into his vehicle, disposing of her phone by throwing it into a river shortly after.

Investigators said Harmel forced the teenager to sleep in a bed with him in his basement, becoming increasingly violent through the 521 days she was held captive. She found her window to escape when the alleged kidnapper granted her access to a phone without cellular data.

Although unable to contact others via traditional means, the device did allow her to use a WiFi connection to play online games. Among Us, which allows players to communicate and was released for mobile devices in 2018, allowed her to get in touch with another child.
After moving the conversation to a different, undisclosed social media app, she then told the other player who she was, revealing that she was actively being held captive at Harmel's home in Oregon.
points: A Utah teenager was rescued from an Oregon man's home after she successfully contacted help from another child in Among Us.

articles.title: Sony Announces Indefinite Delay for PlayStation's Pulse Elevate Wireless Speakers Days Before Launch
articles.summary: Sony has announced an indefinite delay for PlayStation's Pulse Elevate wireless speakers just days before their global launch. The tech company announced the last-minute schedule change in a November 6, 2026, update to an existing PlayStation.Blog post.
body: "As part of our ongoing quality testing of Pulse Elevate speakers, we have identified a production issue with the product and have made the decision to delay the launch," Sony's announcement said. "The additional time will allow us to ensure the product will deliver the experience we intended for our players. We apologize for the delay and appreciate your patience and understanding. We look forward to bringing Pulse Elevate to players soon."

Scroll the tiniest bit further down, and you'll see that Sony had set the Pulse Elevate speakers to launch globally November 12 – just six days out from when the delay update was published. Whatever problem its team encountered must have been pretty significant, but without a new release date or additional information, it's unclear if we'll learn what happened.

articles.title: Path of Exile 2's game director thinks a death recap will finally allow us players to complain about the right things
articles.summary: I've been playing Path of Exile for almost ten years and have put a ton of hours into PoE2 since it entered early access, and in all that time there's one feature that I've wished for more than any other.
body: What I want more than anything is a death recap: a way to finally have some idea why my turbo powerful character that's blasting through a map went pop. At an interview at ExileCon this weekend, game director Jonathan Rogers confirmed that it's finally coming to Path of Exile 2.

I don't know whether Grinding Gear intended to announce the feature this weekend, but during the keynote's live demo of new content, Mark Roberts' character died. And there before our eyes, live and in person, was a death recap screen. After we all got done cheering, Rogers laughed and confirmed that the feature was present and would be included in the full 1.0 release coming up on December 11.

"I was really worried that it wasn't going to be useful enough or accurate enough, but we got it to a place that I'm fairly happy with," Rogers said when I asked him to confirm that the feature would be present at launch.
"The thing that's not quite good is the damage over time tracking," he added. "We do tell you that you took it but we don't know where it came from.”

articles.title: A BioWare documentary was already in the works when the shutdown was announced: 'With the studio's recent closure, the film is now a profound valediction'
articles.summary: Deadline reports that a Canadian documentary about the history of BioWare was already two years into filming when EA closed the studio. Now, it's becoming a sad goodbye to a legendary developer. "The BioWare founders are my hometown heroes," the documentary's writer and director Akash Sherman said.
body: The documentary, Massive Effect: The BioWare Story, features interviews with the studio's founders, Ray Muzyka, Greg Zeschuk, and Augustine Yip, as well as developers Casey Hudson, Mark Darrah, David Gaider, Drew Karpyshyn, Aaryn Flynn, Mac Walters, Trent Oster, James Ohlen, and Caroline Livingstone, voice actor Jennifer Hale, former CEO of EA John Riccitello, and vice president of Lucasfilm Games Douglas Reilly.

Massive Effect: The BioWare Story is scheduled for release next year. Meanwhile, composer Sam Hulick has shared a re-scored version of the leaked trailer for Mass Effect Universe as his own way of saying goodbye, though apparently Amazon's Mass Effect TV series is still in the works.

articles.title: Star Wars Zero Company studio Bit Reactor lays off staff, a month after bringing furloughed developers back
articles.summary: Star Wars Zero Company developer Bit Reactor has laid off an unspecified number of staff, a month after bringing some of its furloughed team back to work.
body: Several developers announced on LinkedIn on Friday, 6th November, that they had been let go, as first reported by Bespin Bulletin. Bit Reactor hasn't said how many people are affected.

Among them is senior environment artist Ryan Lopez, who spent three and a half years working on Zero Company, from pre-production to launch, and was laid off after a three-month furlough. UI engineer Tyler Eichten, who worked on much of the on-screen UI for the game's tactical missions, and Ryan Mosher from the QA team have also confirmed they were let go.
"While it stings, I'm really proud of what we built together," Lopez wrote. "It was a privilege to ship a game with you."

Bit Reactor furloughed most of its staff in the weeks before Zero Company launched on 27th August, with one source putting the figure at roughly 80 percent. The studio appeared to have run out of money just short of release.

articles.title: Chess is immediately more fun if you jettison most of the rules and replace them with weapons-grade Game Boy Advance
articles.summary: I have never been particularly good at The Game of Kings, but I do love when an indie developer turns their talents to turning chess into something more funky. Shotgun King stole my heart a few years ago, and now Rulehouse is looking to offer its own spin on the classic. Weird Weekend.
body: Weird Weekend is our regular Saturday column where we celebrate PC gaming oddities: peculiar games, strange bits of trivia, forgotten history. Pop back every weekend to find out what Jeremy, Josh, Ted, and Rick have become obsessed with this time, whether it's the canon height of Thief's Garrett or that time someone in the Vatican pirated Football Manager.

In a generous demo covering the first act of the game, Rulehouse presents a Wario Ware spin on things⁠—in multiple ways. Each level introduces at least one new mechanic or modifier you have to keep track of, starting with the basic "pawns only, first one to the other side of the board wins," and ramping up to a simulated prison break where guards are firing on your pieces, and you have to get your king⁠—here the game's protagonist in a prison jumpsuit⁠—to the exit.

The escalation in complexity had me genuinely scratching my head, stumped at how to proceed at a few points. Rulehouse eschews trad chess pieces as much as possible, only introducing bishops and kings by the very end of the demo⁠—and stubbornly insisting on calling knights "cows" along the way.
points: I have never been particularly good at The Game of Kings, but I do love when an indie developer turns their talents to turning chess into something more funky.

articles.title: Nintendo's Bill Trinen Explains Why Ocarina Of Time Is The Perfect Entry Point Into The Zelda Universe
articles.summary: Gather round, Kokiri. If you're in a position where you've never actually played a Zelda game before, Nintendo's Bill Trinen just wants to let you know Ocarina of Time is the "perfect place" to start.
body: Although this comment just happens to line up with the arrival of the Switch 2 remake, Nintendo's VP of Player & Product Experience really is convinced this is the best game to begin with, as it's a "foundational story", where the player is taught everything they need to know about the world and characters.

Bill Trinen: "This is the perfect place for your first Zelda game, because you are gonna learn everything that there is about the world and the characters that will serve sort of as the foundation for all the others, all the games that came after.

"This game is sort of a really foundational story for the lore of the Legend of Zelda. It really tells the story of Link and his journey becoming a hero. It tells the story of Link and his connection to Zelda and their relationship with Ganondorf. And overall, it communicates kind of what is at the moral core of is all the series, which is the idea that wisdom and courage combined can overcome power."
points: If you're in a position where you've never actually played a Zelda game before, Nintendo's Bill Trinen just wants to let you know Ocarina of Time is the "perfect place" to start.

articles.title: One of the buggiest D&D games ever released, Pool of Radiance: Ruins of Myth Drannor, is back and actually playable again
articles.summary: "Not since the infamous debut of Daikatana has the release of a single game generated so much incensed indignation from early buyers." Our review of Pool of Radiance: Ruins of Myth Drannor didn't hold back.
body: SNEG's rerelease, available now on Steam and GOG, doesn't have those issues. It adds widescreen, controller support, adjustable combat speed, tooltips, an action bar, and sharpened visuals. If, like me, you skipped this one back in the day because of its reputation for being a hassle to play—even with the eventual patches and community fixes—now it's smooth and problem-free. I've played the opening hours without a single key item vanishing or save file going corrupt.

Don't get the wrong idea, though. Ruins of Myth Drannor isn't Vampire: The Masquerade – Bloodlines. This isn't an RPG masterpiece held back by its buggy release. It's a simplistic turn-based dungeon crawl that's mostly notable for being a spiritual successor to the first Gold Box D&D game, Pool of Radiance, and for adapting the then-new third edition of D&D's rules.

articles.title: Digital Foundry Delivers Its Tech Verdict On Stellar Blade's Switch 2 Port
articles.summary: "Better than expected". Stellar Blade also arrived on the Switch 2 this week, and it's been positively received so far. Here on Nintendo Life, we gave it a score of seven out of ten, and although there are some technical drawbacks, Eve's outing stands tall on the hybrid platform.
body: The team at Digital Foundry has now delivered its tech review of the Unreal Engine 4 title, and while it's no "tour de force", it does translate to a "better than expected Switch 2 port", with what's described as an experience with "gentler compromises" than many more recent titles.

"Technically, it's not a tour de force either, with more conservative visual technology that doesn't leverage current gen hardware like many other high budget titles, but that does translate to a better than expected Switch 2 port, with gentler compromises than many more recent titles. Not everything survives intact, but the game's visual character isn't disrupted by the excision of key lighting systems or anything like that. Instead, players can expect a range of more iterative asset downgrades, some of which only really stand out in head-to-heads."

As for frame generation, on Switch 2, Digital Foundry says it's "not a bad choice considering the CPU and GPU limits of the console", but in the case of Stellar Blade, a "40fps targeting option" may have offered a better experience than the 60fps output with frame gen on. You can also turn frame gen "off" and the game will hover around the 40fps mark.
points: Stellar Blade also arrived on the Switch 2 this week, and it's been positively received so far.
